paragraphs: Abraham believed, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness; Paul hears in that old verdict a blessing already leaning toward the nations. A curse hangs on a tree, and through that very tree the blessing is carried out, so that a promise made to one aged man arrives as the Spirit given to everyone who trusts. The psalmist keeps a quieter ledger: the Lord is mindful of his covenant, his works are remembered. Newman saw that to a heart given over to God, command and promise are one thing.

The Gospel lets us look inside a house. A strong man guards his palace, a stronger one strips him of the armor he trusted, and a swept, garnished dwelling stands vacant, the most dangerous condition of all. Tradition hears in “the finger of God” the Spirit himself, who once wrote on stone and now writes on hearts.

quote.text: the prince of this world, who works in the children of disobedience by no other power than the fellowship and the bond of sin, is cast out by our faith.
quote.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 21 on the New Testament Lessons (Ben. 71), on Matthew 12, the parallel to Luke 11:15–26, §19
quote.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6 (ed. P. Schaff)

closing: No one stands neutral here: whoever does not gather, scatters. Better to be occupied by the promise than merely tidy.
